# Was the USDA farm payment system outage a hack?

**Reported.** A USDA under secretary calls it a cyberthreat. NBC and ABC sources say outsiders got in, but he says defenses worked. Whether anyone actually got in is not settled.

Incident: USDA farm payment system cyberattack, Nov 2026. Also reported as the USDA hack and the USDA cybersecurity incident. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 12:14 AM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by USDA, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 12:14 AM ET: **USDA says a cyberthreat hit farm loan and payment systems; anonymous sources say hackers got in, USDA says defenses worked.** First draft. 5 sources (0 Tier 1), 12 claims (5 Confirmed, 3 Reported, 4 Not established), 6 questions. No written USDA statement found. An under secretary spoke on the record; the break-in itself rests on anonymous sources and is contradicted by that official, so the main question is Reported. Privacy check done: no individuals named, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Nation-level. Farm Service Agency offices across the US reported outages in loan, payment and mapping tools for about a week, ahead of a Dec 11 sign-up deadline. The number of farmers affected is not given.
- Who is affected: Farmers and ranchers who use USDA loan, payment and conservation programs, and USDA staff. USDA says no personal information was involved.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| ~1 week | Disruption so far | Since about Nov 16 |
| None | Personal data, USDA says | An official's statement |

### Known so far

- A USDA under secretary called the week-long disruption a cyberthreat, not a software update.
- Loan, payment and mapping tools went down, delaying farmer loans and payments.
- The disruption began around Monday, Nov 16.
- The under secretary says no personal information was involved and no data was lost.

### Not known yet

- Whether outsiders actually got into the payment system.
- Who was behind it.
- Whether any data was taken.
- Whether every system is back online.
